# 2 Baruch Chapter 14 — Disagreement Log
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Date:** 2026-03-17

---

## 14:6-8 — Structure of existential complaint

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | Full Syriac compound sentences with connectives | Literal chain; preserves Syriac sentence structure |
| LOGOS | Formal English with conjunctions preserved | Formal chain |
| PNEUMA | Short declarative sentences for impact | Modern rhetorical structure |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** LOGOS adopted. The Syriac here uses a deliberate chain of connected clauses that mirror the accumulation of despair. PNEUMA's short sentences create modern punch but lose the cumulative syntactic weight.

---

## 14:9 — "held back from creating" vs. "regretted creating"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "held-back-from-creating-man" | Literal |
| LOGOS | "held back from creating man" | Formal |
| PNEUMA | "regretted creating humanity" | "Regretted" — more direct but theologically different |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** LOGOS adopted. The Syriac verb here means 'to withhold' or 'to refrain from,' not 'to repent of.' The question is whether God would have been better off not creating humans — not whether God regrets having created them. PNEUMA introduces anthropopathism not present in the source.

---

## 14:11 — "firstborn" and "whom you have loved"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "whom-you-called-your-firstborn, whom-you-have-beloved" | Literal two-part appellation |
| LOGOS | "whom you called your firstborn and whom you have loved" | Formal, two relative clauses |
| PNEUMA | "a people you loved, calling them firstborn" | Reorders and conflates |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** LOGOS adopted. The two relative clauses are distinct: (1) the formal title "firstborn" given to Israel (Exod 4:22), and (2) the statement of divine love. PNEUMA's conflation loses the formal naming act.

---

## 14:14 — "You do not rejoice in the things which you have made"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "You-do-not-rejoice-in-the-things-which-you-have-made" | Literal divine emotion statement |
| LOGOS | "You do not rejoice in the things which you have made" | Formal |
| PNEUMA | "You take no delight in what you have made" | "Delight" for "rejoice" — slightly stronger connotation |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** LOGOS adopted. "Rejoice in" is the standard Syriac verb for divine pleasure in creation (cf. Gen 1 "God saw that it was good"). "Delight" is acceptable but edges toward a stronger connotation.

---

**Total disagreements this chapter: 4**
